plan.text:
Objective: maximise bank balance by day 30 (start €1500). Rent €12/day spot fee. Cash reserve: keep >= €300 always. Targets: D5-9 stock first machines; weekly revenue rising. Restock = 45min each, so only ~8 slot fills/day: prioritise high-selling products in the best slots.
Suppliers: bakker-en-zoon (stroopwafel, choco, crisps, nuts, cola, oat latte; cheapest), zuidas-groothandel (sparkling, energy, gummy, tortilla, mint, dropjes; cheapest for water/energy), noordzee-dranken (bev, min €90).

scorecard.text: Day 30 (final): cash €2386.26 at 09:00 (card receipts still to settle). Units ~982, revenue ~2373. No open complaints. Ending run.

rules.text:
- Deliveries appear the morning AFTER due day (e.g., PO due 16 shows day 17). Count lag +1 day.
- Stock-outs cost the most: order ~2 weeks ahead; keep 1 full batch always in depot, not just on arrival day.
- Restock is the bottleneck: ~7 fills/day. Use 18-unit small slots for volume (gummy, mint, choco, stroop, nuts); large slots only for tortilla/crisps (10).
- Zuidas prices drop 30% some weeks (tortilla 1.65, crisps 1.38, mint 0.60): buy then, several weeks of stock.
- Refusals: order refused if below minimum or insufficient funds; recheck offers first.
- Customer complaints: refund CMP refs promptly (done once day 13).

experiments.text:
Day 15: AI-HOUSE tortilla price 3.20 -> 3.60 (AI-HOUSE less price-sensitive). Measure: AI-HOUSE tortilla units/day vs ~3-4 before. If volume holds, keep; else revert 3.20.
Day 15 3-day sales: tortilla 25 (~€3.19 avg) top; gummy 11; oat 5; energy 5; crisps 4 (stock-outs); nuts 6; cola 5; mint 5; choco 2; sparkling 2.
